page: Amazon Web Services m7i.metal-24xl is a general-purpose, bare-metal server engineered around the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz, the configuration offers 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 384 GB, maintaining an even 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution typical of general-purpose profiles. Networking capabilities include a 38 Gbps baseline bandwidth, though the server includes no onboard local instance storage and provisions no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing indicates exceptional multi-threaded performance driven by its non-virtualized core density. The server achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,748 and a PassMark CPU score of 88,761, both ranking in the top ten percent of tested cloud hardware. Heavy multi-threaded tasks excel noticeably, evidenced by top-tier results in Clang software compilation (58,304) and ray tracing (96,325). The processor incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 instructions, which support CPU-based machine learning inference, demonstrated by prompt processing rates reaching 292.47 tokens per second on 7B models. Cryptographic throughput is similarly top-tier, scoring 90,696.93 on PassMark encryption tests.

Because the m7i.metal-24xl operates directly on bare metal without a hypervisor layer, it removes virtualization contention and timing variances. The primary operational tradeoff is the complete reliance on network-attached storage, as the lack of local NVMe drives shifts high-IOPS disk requirements entirely onto network storage infrastructure. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform yields high compute and memory density per socket, making it practical for organizations consolidating massive virtualization hosts, running large container clusters, executing automated build and test pipelines, or deploying high-throughput in-memory datastores such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical Intel Xeon 8488C cores running at 3.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with a substantial 105 MB L3 cache, the system supplies 384 GB of system memory, conforming to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Network throughput reaches a 38 Gbps baseline, while local storage is absent, requiring external storage volumes for stateful persistence. Operating without a hypervisor, it enables direct hardware access with hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate top-decile multi-core capabilities, registering an 88,761 PassMark CPU score and 21,748 in multi-core Geekbench, alongside strong performance in Clang software compilation and cryptographic execution. The instance delivers high resource density for computationally demanding, multi-threaded workloads, making it well fitted for continuous integration pipelines, heavy container orchestration, distributed caching clusters, and enterprise application servers requiring predictable execution without hypervisor jitter.
